raw: Act 3, Scene 1 — A public Place

sentences.en: A public Place
sentences.ko: 광장

summary.en: Tybalt wants to fight Romeo, but Romeo refuses. Mercutio fights instead and is killed. Romeo kills Tybalt, and the Prince banishes Romeo.
summary.ko: 티볼트가 로미오와 싸우려 하지만 로미오는 거절한다. 대신 머큐쇼가 싸우다 죽는다. 로미오는 티볼트를 죽이고, 영주는 로미오를 추방한다.

raw: Enter Mercutio, Benvolio, Page and Servants.

sentences.en: Mercutio, Benvolio, a Page, and Servants enter.
sentences.ko: 머큐쇼, 벤볼리오, 시동, 그리고 하인들이 들어온다.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
I pray thee, good Mercutio, let’s retire:
The day is hot, the Capulets abroad,
And if we meet, we shall not scape a brawl,
For now these hot days, is the mad blood stirring.

sentences.en: Please, good Mercutio, let us go home.
sentences.ko: 머큐쇼, 제발 이제 들어가자.

sentences.en: The day is hot.
sentences.ko: 날씨가 너무 덥네.

sentences.en: The Capulets are out and about.
sentences.ko: 캐퓰릿 사람들이 나돌아 다녀.

sentences.en: If we meet them, we will not escape a fight.
sentences.ko: 그들과 마주치면 싸움을 피할 수 없을 거야.

sentences.en: These hot days make people's blood boil and make them angry.
sentences.ko: 이 더운 날씨는 사람들의 피를 끓게 하고 화나게 만든단 말이야.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Thou art like one of these fellows that, when he enters the confines of
a tavern, claps me his sword upon the table, and says ‘God send me no
need of thee!’ and by the operation of the second cup draws him on the
drawer, when indeed there is no need.

sentences.en: You are like one of those men.
sentences.ko: 너는 딱 그런 녀석들 같아.

sentences.en: When they enter a tavern, they put their sword on the table.
sentences.ko: 그들은 술집에 들어오면 탁자 위에 칼을 올려놓지.

sentences.en: They say, 'God send me no need of you!'
sentences.ko: '하나님, 이 칼 쓸 일이 없게 해 주소서!'라고 하지.

sentences.en: After the second drink, they draw their sword on the barman.
sentences.ko: 두 잔째 마시고는 술집 주인한테 칼을 뽑지.

sentences.en: They do this even when there is no need for it.
sentences.ko: 꼭 필요하지 않은 상황에서도 그러는 거야.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Am I like such a fellow?

sentences.en: Am I like such a man?
sentences.ko: 내가 그런 사람 같다고?

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Come, come, thou art as hot a Jack in thy mood as any in Italy; and as
soon moved to be moody, and as soon moody to be moved.

sentences.en: Come, come, you are as hot-headed as any man in Italy.
sentences.ko: 자, 자, 넌 이탈리아에서 제일가는 성질 급한 놈이야.

sentences.en: You get angry very quickly.
sentences.ko: 너는 아주 금방 화를 내지.

sentences.en: And you become calm just as quickly.
sentences.ko: 그리고 똑같이 빨리 진정하기도 하고.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: And what to?

sentences.en: Moved to what?
sentences.ko: 무엇 때문에 움직인다는 거야?

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Nay, an there were two such, we should have none shortly, for one would
kill the other. Thou? Why, thou wilt quarrel with a man that hath a
hair more or a hair less in his beard than thou hast. Thou wilt quarrel
with a man for cracking nuts, having no other reason but because thou
hast hazel eyes. What eye but such an eye would spy out such a quarrel?
Thy head is as full of quarrels as an egg is full of meat, and yet thy
head hath been beaten as addle as an egg for quarrelling. Thou hast
quarrelled with a man for coughing in the street, because he hath
wakened thy dog that hath lain asleep in the sun. Didst thou not fall
out with a tailor for wearing his new doublet before Easter? with
another for tying his new shoes with an old riband? And yet thou wilt
tutor me from quarrelling!

sentences.en: No, if there were two such men, we would have none of them soon.
sentences.ko: 아니, 그런 놈이 둘이면 곧 하나도 안 남겠지.

sentences.en: One would kill the other.
sentences.ko: 한 명이 다른 한 명을 죽일 테니까.

sentences.en: You? You would fight a man who has one hair more or less in his beard than you.
sentences.ko: 너 말이야? 턱수염이 너보다 한 가닥 많거나 적다는 이유로도 싸움을 벌이는 놈이잖아.

sentences.en: You would fight a man for cracking nuts.
sentences.ko: 호두를 깐다는 이유로도 싸우겠지.

sentences.en: You would do this for no reason other than because you have hazel eyes.
sentences.ko: 네 눈이 호두색이라는 이유 하나로 말이야.

sentences.en: What eye but such an eye would find such a fight?
sentences.ko: 그런 눈이 아니면 누가 이런 싸움을 찾겠어?

sentences.en: Your head is as full of fights as an egg is full of meat.
sentences.ko: 네 머리엔 달걀에 속이 꽉 찬 것처럼 싸움이 꽉 차 있어.

sentences.en: Yet your head has been beaten as soft as an egg from fighting.
sentences.ko: 하지만 그 머리는 너무 많이 싸우는 바람에 달걀처럼 말랑해졌고.

sentences.en: You fought a man for coughing in the street.
sentences.ko: 거리에서 기침했다고 사람하고 싸운 적도 있잖아.

sentences.en: He had woken up your dog that was sleeping in the sun.
sentences.ko: 그 사람이 햇볕 아래 자고 있던 네 개를 깨웠기 때문이지.

sentences.en: Did you not fight with a tailor for wearing his new jacket before Easter?
sentences.ko: 부활절도 되기 전에 새 옷을 입었다고 재단사와 싸우지 않았어?

sentences.en: Did you not fight with another for tying his new shoes with an old ribbon?
sentences.ko: 새 신발을 낡은 리본으로 묶었다는 이유로 다른 사람과 싸우지도 않았고.

sentences.en: And yet you want to tell me not to fight!
sentences.ko: 그런데 이제 나더러 싸우지 말라고 하겠다니!

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
And I were so apt to quarrel as thou art, any man should buy the fee
simple of my life for an hour and a quarter.

sentences.en: Suppose I were as ready to fight as you are.
sentences.ko: 내가 너만큼 싸울 준비가 되어 있다고 가정해 봐.

sentences.en: Then any man could buy full ownership of my life for an hour and a quarter.
sentences.ko: 그럼 누구든 한 시간 십오 분이면 내 목숨을 통째로 살 수 있겠지.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: The fee simple! O simple!

sentences.en: Full ownership!
sentences.ko: 통째로라니!

sentences.en: How simple-minded!
sentences.ko: 참 단순하기도 하지!

raw: Enter Tybalt and others.

sentences.en: Tybalt and others enter.
sentences.ko: 티볼트와 다른 이들이 들어온다.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: By my head, here comes the Capulets.

sentences.en: By my head, here come the Capulets.
sentences.ko: 맹세코, 캐퓰릿 놈들이 온다.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: By my heel, I care not.

sentences.en: By my heel, I do not care.
sentences.ko: 맹세코, 난 상관없어.

speaker: TYBALT
raw:
Follow me close, for I will speak to them.
Gentlemen, good-den: a word with one of you.

sentences.en: Follow me closely because I will speak to them.
sentences.ko: 바짝 따라와라. 내가 저들에게 말을 걸 테니.

sentences.en: Good evening, gentlemen; I want a word with one of you.
sentences.ko: 안녕하시오, 신사분들. 한 사람에게 할 말이 있소.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
And but one word with one of us? Couple it with something; make it a
word and a blow.

sentences.en: Only one word with one of us?
sentences.ko: 우리 중 한 명과 단 한 마디라니?

sentences.en: Add something else to it.
sentences.ko: 거기에 다른 것도 좀 얹어봐.

sentences.en: Make it a word and a blow.
sentences.ko: 말 한마디에 한 방을 곁들여.

speaker: TYBALT
raw:
You shall find me apt enough to that, sir, and you will give me
occasion.

sentences.en: You will find me ready enough for that, sir, if you give me a reason.
sentences.ko: 이유만 대준다면 나도 기꺼이 응해주지.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: Could you not take some occasion without giving?

sentences.en: Could you not take a reason without being given one?
sentences.ko: 이유를 받지 않고는 못 찾아내나?

speaker: TYBALT
raw: Mercutio, thou consortest with Romeo.

sentences.en: Mercutio, you are spending time with Romeo.
sentences.ko: 머큐쇼, 넌 로미오와 한패로 어울리는군.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Consort? What, dost thou make us minstrels? And thou make minstrels of
us, look to hear nothing but discords. Here’s my fiddlestick, here’s
that shall make you dance. Zounds, consort!

sentences.en: Spend time? What, do you think we are musicians?
sentences.ko: 한패? 뭐야, 우릴 악단으로 아나?

sentences.en: If you make us musicians, expect to hear only bad notes.
sentences.ko: 우리를 음악가로 취급한다면 엉망인 연주를 듣게 될 거다.

sentences.en: You will only hear unpleasant sounds.
sentences.ko: 불쾌한 소리만 들릴 뿐이지.

sentences.en: This sword is my fiddle stick.
sentences.ko: 이 칼이 내 바이올린 활이다.

sentences.en: Here is what will make you dance.
sentences.ko: 자, 이제 네가 춤을 추게 될 거다.

sentences.en: Damn it, 'spend time'!
sentences.ko: 빌어먹을, '한패'라니!

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
We talk here in the public haunt of men.
Either withdraw unto some private place,
And reason coldly of your grievances,
Or else depart; here all eyes gaze on us.

sentences.en: We are talking here in a public place.
sentences.ko: 우리는 지금 공공장소에 있어.

sentences.en: Either go to a private place.
sentences.ko: 사적인 장소로 가든가.

sentences.en: Talk about your problems calmly there.
sentences.ko: 거기서 차분하게 따지든가.

sentences.en: Or leave now.
sentences.ko: 아니면 지금 떠나고.

sentences.en: Everyone is looking at us here.
sentences.ko: 모두가 우리를 보고 있어.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Men’s eyes were made to look, and let them gaze.
I will not budge for no man’s pleasure, I.

sentences.en: Men's eyes were made to look.
sentences.ko: 사람 눈은 보라고 있는 거야.

sentences.en: Let them look.
sentences.ko: 그들이 보게 내버려 둬.

sentences.en: I will not move for any man's pleasure.
sentences.ko: 누가 뭐래도 난 한 발짝도 안 움직여.

raw: Enter Romeo.

speaker: TYBALT
raw: Well, peace be with you, sir, here comes my man.

sentences.en: Well, peace be with you, sir.
sentences.ko: 좋아, 너와는 이만.

sentences.en: Here comes my man.
sentences.ko: 내 상대가 온다.

speaker: MERCUTIO

sentences.en: But I will be hanged if he wears your uniform.
sentences.ko: 그놈이 네 하인 옷을 입었다면 내 목을 매달겠다.

sentences.en: But go to the dueling field first.
sentences.ko: 먼저 결투장으로 가 봐.

sentences.en: He will follow you there.
sentences.ko: 그가 거기로 따라올 테니까.

sentences.en: Only in that sense can you call him your man.
sentences.ko: 그런 뜻에서라면 그를 네 '사람'이라 부를 수 있겠지.

speaker: TYBALT
raw:
Romeo, the love I bear thee can afford
No better term than this: Thou art a villain.

sentences.en: Romeo, the love I have for you allows no better word than this.
sentences.ko: 로미오, 너에 대한 내 사랑으론 이 말밖에 할 말이 없다.

sentences.en: You are a villain.
sentences.ko: 너는 악당이야.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Tybalt, the reason that I have to love thee
Doth much excuse the appertaining rage
To such a greeting. Villain am I none;
Therefore farewell; I see thou know’st me not.

sentences.en: Tybalt, I have a reason to love you.
sentences.ko: 티볼트, 내가 너를 사랑하는 이유가 있어.

sentences.en: It lets me forgive the anger I should feel at such a greeting.
sentences.ko: 그 덕분에 이런 인사에 느껴야 할 분노를 용서할 수 있어.

sentences.en: I am not a villain.
sentences.ko: 나는 악당이 아니야.

sentences.en: Therefore goodbye.
sentences.ko: 그러니 잘 가라.

sentences.en: I see that you do not know me.
sentences.ko: 넌 나를 모르는구나.

speaker: TYBALT
raw:
Boy, this shall not excuse the injuries
That thou hast done me, therefore turn and draw.

sentences.en: Boy, this will not excuse the injuries you have done to me.
sentences.ko: 이 녀석, 그런다고 네가 내게 준 모욕이 용서되진 않아.

sentences.en: Therefore turn and draw your sword.
sentences.ko: 그러니 몸을 돌려 칼을 뽑아라.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
I do protest I never injur’d thee,
But love thee better than thou canst devise
Till thou shalt know the reason of my love.
And so good Capulet, which name I tender
As dearly as mine own, be satisfied.

sentences.en: I protest that I never hurt you.
sentences.ko: 맹세코 난 널 모욕한 적이 없어.

sentences.en: I love you more than you can imagine.
sentences.ko: 네가 상상하는 것보다 훨씬 더 너를 아껴.

sentences.en: You will see this when you know the reason for my love.
sentences.ko: 내 사랑의 이유를 알게 되면 이해할 거야.

sentences.en: And since I value the name Capulet as much as my own, be satisfied.
sentences.ko: 그러니 캐퓰릿, 내 이름만큼 소중한 그 이름을 생각해서, 이만 참아 줘.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: O calm, dishonourable, vile submission!

sentences.en: Oh, what a calm, dishonorable, and vile submission!
sentences.ko: 오, 이 얌전하고, 비겁하고, 비굴한 굴복이라니!

raw: Draws.

sentences.en: Mercutio draws his sword.
sentences.ko: 머큐쇼가 칼을 뽑는다.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Alla stoccata carries it away.
Tybalt, you rat-catcher, will you walk?

sentences.en: So this fancy fighting man wins, does he?
sentences.ko: 결국 칼솜씨 뽐내는 놈이 이긴단 말이지?

sentences.en: Tybalt, you rat-catcher, will you come and fight?
sentences.ko: 티볼트, 이 쥐잡이 녀석아, 나랑 한판 붙을래?

speaker: TYBALT
raw: What wouldst thou have with me?

sentences.en: What do you want from me?
sentences.ko: 나한테 원하는 게 뭐야?

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Good King of Cats, nothing but one of your nine lives; that I mean to
make bold withal, and, as you shall use me hereafter, dry-beat the rest
of the eight. Will you pluck your sword out of his pilcher by the ears?
Make haste, lest mine be about your ears ere it be out.

sentences.en: Good King of Cats, I only need one of your nine lives.
sentences.ko: 고양이 왕 나으리, 네 목숨 아홉 개 중 하나만 받아 가면 돼.

sentences.en: I intend to be bold with it.
sentences.ko: 그걸로 용감하게 승부할 생각이야.

sentences.en: And then I will beat the other eight out of you.
sentences.ko: 그러고 나서 나머지 여덟 개를 다 뺏어버릴 거야.

sentences.en: Will you pull your sword out of its case by the ears?
sentences.ko: 칼집에서 칼을 귀 잡고 끌어낼 참이야?

sentences.en: Hurry, or my sword will be around your ears before yours is out.
sentences.ko: 서둘러, 안 그러면 네 칼이 나오기도 전에 내 칼이 네 귀를 스칠 거다.

raw: Drawing.

sentences.en: Tybalt draws his sword.
sentences.ko: 티볼트가 칼을 뽑는다.

speaker: TYBALT
raw: I am for you.

sentences.en: I am ready to fight you.
sentences.ko: 상대해 주마.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Gentle Mercutio, put thy rapier up.

sentences.en: Gentle Mercutio, put your sword away.
sentences.ko: 다정한 머큐쇼, 칼을 집어넣어.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: Come, sir, your passado.

sentences.en: Come, sir, show me your fancy move.
sentences.ko: 자, 네 그 멋진 찌르기를 보여 줘 봐.

raw: They fight.

sentences.en: They fight.
sentences.ko: 그들이 싸운다.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Draw, Benvolio; beat down their weapons.
Gentlemen, for shame, forbear this outrage,
Tybalt, Mercutio, the Prince expressly hath
Forbid this bandying in Verona streets.
Hold, Tybalt! Good Mercutio!

sentences.en: Draw, Benvolio, and beat down their weapons.
sentences.ko: 벤볼리오, 칼을 뽑아 저들의 칼을 쳐 내!

sentences.en: Gentlemen, stop this violence for shame!
sentences.ko: 신사들, 창피하지도 않나, 이 난동을 멈춰!

sentences.en: Tybalt, Mercutio, the Prince has strictly forbidden fighting in the streets of Verona.
sentences.ko: 티볼트, 머큐쇼, 영주께서 베로나 거리에서의 싸움을 엄격히 금지하셨다.

sentences.en: Stop, Tybalt! Good Mercutio!
sentences.ko: 멈춰, 티볼트! 머큐쇼!

raw: Exeunt Tybalt with his Partizans.

sentences.en: Tybalt runs off with his followers.
sentences.ko: 티볼트가 부하들과 함께 달려 나간다.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
I am hurt.
A plague o’ both your houses. I am sped.
Is he gone, and hath nothing?

sentences.en: I am hurt. A plague on both your houses.
sentences.ko: 찔렸어. 너희 두 집안 모두 염병에나 걸려라!

sentences.en: I am dying. Is he gone without a scratch?
sentences.ko: 난 끝났어. 그놈은 상처 하나 없이 갔나?

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: What, art thou hurt?

sentences.en: What, are you hurt?
sentences.ko: 뭐라고, 너 다쳤어?

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Ay, ay, a scratch, a scratch. Marry, ’tis enough.
Where is my page? Go villain, fetch a surgeon.

sentences.en: Yes, yes, it is just a scratch; it is enough.
sentences.ko: 그래, 그래, 살짝 긁힌 것뿐이야. 이 정도면 충분해.

sentences.en: Where is my servant? Go, boy, and get a doctor.
sentences.ko: 내 시동은 어디 있지? 얘야, 가서 의사를 불러와.

raw: Exit Page.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Courage, man; the hurt cannot be much.

sentences.en: Be brave, man.
sentences.ko: 힘내, 친구.

sentences.en: The injury cannot be very bad.
sentences.ko: 상처가 그리 심각하진 않을 거야.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
No, ’tis not so deep as a well, nor so wide as a church door, but ’tis
enough, ’twill serve. Ask for me tomorrow, and you shall find me a
grave man. I am peppered, I warrant, for this world. A plague o’ both
your houses. Zounds, a dog, a rat, a mouse, a cat, to scratch a man to
death. A braggart, a rogue, a villain, that fights by the book of
arithmetic!—Why the devil came you between us? I was hurt under your
arm.

sentences.en: No, it is not as deep as a well or as wide as a church door.
sentences.ko: 아니, 우물처럼 깊지도 교회 문처럼 넓지도 않아.

sentences.en: But it is enough; it will do.
sentences.ko: 하지만 충분해, 이 정도면 됐어.

sentences.en: Ask for me tomorrow, and you will find me a grave man lying in my grave.
sentences.ko: 내일 나를 찾아봐. 무덤 속의 점잖은 사람이 되어 있을 테니.

sentences.en: I am finished in this world, I promise. A plague on both your houses.
sentences.ko: 난 이 세상에선 끝났어. 너희 두 집안 모두 염병에나 걸려라!

sentences.en: To think a dog, a rat, a mouse, or a cat could scratch a man to death!
sentences.ko: 개나 쥐, 생쥐, 혹은 고양이가 사람을 할퀴어 죽일 수도 있다니!

sentences.en: He is a show-off and a rogue; he is a villain who fights by a math textbook!
sentences.ko: 그놈은 허풍쟁이에 악당이고, 산수책대로 칼질하는 놈이야!

sentences.en: Why did you come between us? I was hurt under your arm.
sentences.ko: 넌 왜 끼어들었어? 네 팔 밑으로 찔렸잖아.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: I thought all for the best.

sentences.en: I thought it was for the best.
sentences.ko: 그게 최선이라고 생각했어.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Help me into some house, Benvolio,
Or I shall faint. A plague o’ both your houses.
They have made worms’ meat of me.
I have it, and soundly too. Your houses!

sentences.en: Help me into a house, Benvolio, or I will faint.
sentences.ko: 벤볼리오, 나를 집 안으로 옮겨줘, 아니면 쓰러질 것 같아.

sentences.en: A plague on both your houses!
sentences.ko: 너희 두 집안 모두 염병에나 걸려라!

sentences.en: They have made me food for worms.
sentences.ko: 그들이 날 벌레들의 먹이로 만들었어.

sentences.en: I have got it, and badly too.
sentences.ko: 제대로 당했어, 아주 지독하게.

sentences.en: Your houses!
sentences.ko: 너희 집안들!

raw: Exeunt Mercutio and Benvolio.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
This gentleman, the Prince’s near ally,
My very friend, hath got his mortal hurt
In my behalf; my reputation stain’d
With Tybalt’s slander,—Tybalt, that an hour
Hath been my cousin. O sweet Juliet,
Thy beauty hath made me effeminate
And in my temper soften’d valour’s steel.

sentences.en: This gentleman is the Prince's close relative.
sentences.ko: 이분은 영주님의 가까운 친척이다.

sentences.en: He is my very friend.
sentences.ko: 그는 나의 아주 소중한 친구다.

sentences.en: He suffered a fatal injury for me.
sentences.ko: 그는 나를 위해 치명적인 상처를 입었다.

sentences.en: My reputation is ruined by Tybalt's lies.
sentences.ko: 티볼트의 거짓말 때문에 내 명예가 더럽혀졌다.

sentences.en: Tybalt has been my cousin for only an hour!
sentences.ko: 티볼트는 겨우 한 시간 전에 내 사촌이 되었는데!

sentences.en: Oh sweet Juliet, your beauty has made me weak.
sentences.ko: 오 사랑스러운 줄리엣, 그대의 아름다움이 나를 나약하게 만들었다.

sentences.en: It softened my brave spirit.
sentences.ko: 내 용기의 칼날을 무디게 했다.

raw: Re-enter Benvolio.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
O Romeo, Romeo, brave Mercutio’s dead,
That gallant spirit hath aspir’d the clouds,
Which too untimely here did scorn the earth.

sentences.en: Oh Romeo, Romeo, brave Mercutio is dead.
sentences.ko: 오 로미오, 로미오, 용감한 머큐쇼가 죽었어.

sentences.en: His brave spirit has gone up to the clouds.
sentences.ko: 그의 용감한 영혼은 구름 위로 올라갔어.

sentences.en: He left the earth far too early.
sentences.ko: 그는 너무 일찍 이 세상을 떠났어.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
This day’s black fate on mo days doth depend;
This but begins the woe others must end.

sentences.en: This day's dark fate will hang over more days to come.
sentences.ko: 오늘의 어두운 운명이 앞으로 올 날들까지 덮칠 거야.

sentences.en: This only begins the sadness that others must end.
sentences.ko: 이건 다른 날들이 끝맺어야 할 비극의 시작일 뿐이야.

raw: Re-enter Tybalt.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Here comes the furious Tybalt back again.

sentences.en: The angry Tybalt is coming back here.
sentences.ko: 화가 난 티볼트가 이쪽으로 오고 있어.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Again in triumph, and Mercutio slain?
Away to heaven respective lenity,
And fire-ey’d fury be my conduct now!
Now, Tybalt, take the ‘villain’ back again
That late thou gav’st me, for Mercutio’s soul
Is but a little way above our heads,
Staying for thine to keep him company.
Either thou or I, or both, must go with him.

sentences.en: He is alive and winning, and Mercutio is dead?
sentences.ko: 그놈은 살아남아 승리했는데, 머큐쇼는 죽었다고?

sentences.en: I will not be gentle now.
sentences.ko: 이제 너그러움은 하늘로 가 버려라.

sentences.en: I will act with fire and anger!
sentences.ko: 불타는 분노여, 나를 이끌어라!

sentences.en: Now, Tybalt, take back the 'villain' title.
sentences.ko: 자, 티볼트, 이제 '악당'이라는 칭호를 네가 가져가라.

sentences.en: You gave me that name recently.
sentences.ko: 네가 얼마 전에 나에게 그 이름을 붙여줬지.

sentences.en: Mercutio's soul is just above our heads.
sentences.ko: 머큐쇼의 영혼이 바로 우리 머리 위에 있어.

sentences.en: He is waiting for your soul to join him.
sentences.ko: 네 영혼이 함께 가 주기를 기다리고 있다.

sentences.en: Either you or I, or both of us, must go with him.
sentences.ko: 너나 나, 혹은 우리 둘 다 그와 함께 가야 해.

speaker: TYBALT
raw:
Thou wretched boy, that didst consort him here,
Shalt with him hence.

sentences.en: You miserable boy, you were his friend here.
sentences.ko: 이 비참한 녀석, 여기서 그놈과 어울렸으니

sentences.en: So you will go with him to death.
sentences.ko: 그놈과 함께 저승으로 가라.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: This shall determine that.

sentences.en: This will decide that.
sentences.ko: 이 칼이 정해 줄 거다.

raw: They fight; Tybalt falls.

sentences.en: They fight.
sentences.ko: 그들이 싸운다.

sentences.en: Tybalt falls.
sentences.ko: 티볼트가 쓰러진다.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
Romeo, away, be gone!
The citizens are up, and Tybalt slain.
Stand not amaz’d. The Prince will doom thee death
If thou art taken. Hence, be gone, away!

sentences.en: Romeo, go away! The citizens are up in arms.
sentences.ko: 로미오, 도망쳐! 시민들이 들고일어났어.

sentences.en: Tybalt is killed, so do not stand there in shock.
sentences.ko: 티볼트가 죽었으니 멍하니 서 있지 마.

sentences.en: The Prince will sentence you to death if he catches you.
sentences.ko: 영주가 너를 발견하면 사형에 처할 거야.

sentences.en: Go away now!
sentences.ko: 당장 여기서 떠나!

speaker: ROMEO
raw: O, I am fortune’s fool!

sentences.en: Oh, I am a plaything of fate!
sentences.ko: 아, 나는 운명의 노리개구나!

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Why dost thou stay?

sentences.en: Why do you stay?
sentences.ko: 왜 아직 여기 있어?

raw: Exit Romeo.
Enter Citizens.

sentences.en: Citizens enter.
sentences.ko: 시민들이 들어온다.

speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
raw:
Which way ran he that kill’d Mercutio?
Tybalt, that murderer, which way ran he?

sentences.en: In which direction did the man who killed Mercutio run?
sentences.ko: 머큐쇼를 죽인 자가 어느 방향으로 도망쳤습니까?

sentences.en: Tybalt, that murderer, which way did he run?
sentences.ko: 그 살인자 티볼트 말입니다, 어느 쪽으로 도망갔습니까?

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: There lies that Tybalt.

sentences.en: That is Tybalt lying there.
sentences.ko: 저기 쓰러져 있는 게 바로 티볼트야.

speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
raw:
Up, sir, go with me.
I charge thee in the Prince’s name obey.

sentences.en: Get up, sir.
sentences.ko: 일어나십시오.

sentences.en: Come with me.
sentences.ko: 저와 함께 가시지요.

sentences.en: I command you in the Prince's name to obey.
sentences.ko: 영주님의 이름으로 명령하니 따르십시오.

raw: Enter Prince, attended; Montague, Capulet, their Wives and others.

sentences.en: The Prince enters with his followers.
sentences.ko: 영주가 부하들과 함께 들어온다.

sentences.en: Montague, Capulet, their wives, and others enter.
sentences.ko: 몬태규, 캐퓰릿, 그들의 아내들, 그리고 다른 이들이 들어온다.

speaker: PRINCE
raw: Where are the vile beginners of this fray?

sentences.en: Where are the people who started this fight?
sentences.ko: 이 싸움을 시작한 자들이 어디 있느냐?

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
O noble Prince, I can discover all
The unlucky manage of this fatal brawl.
There lies the man, slain by young Romeo,
That slew thy kinsman, brave Mercutio.

sentences.en: Noble Prince, I can explain everything.
sentences.ko: 고귀하신 영주님, 제가 모든 것을 설명할 수 있습니다.

sentences.en: I can tell you how this deadly fight happened.
sentences.ko: 이 치명적인 싸움이 어떻게 일어났는지 말씀드릴 수 있습니다.

sentences.en: There lies the man who killed your relative, brave Mercutio.
sentences.ko: 저기 영주님의 친척, 용감한 머큐쇼를 죽인 자가 누워 있습니다.

sentences.en: Young Romeo killed him.
sentences.ko: 젊은 로미오가 그자를 죽였습니다.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Tybalt, my cousin! O my brother’s child!
O Prince! O husband! O, the blood is spill’d
Of my dear kinsman! Prince, as thou art true,
For blood of ours shed blood of Montague.
O cousin, cousin.

sentences.en: Tybalt, my nephew! He is my brother's child!
sentences.ko: 티볼트, 내 조카! 오라버니의 아들이!

sentences.en: O Prince! O husband! The blood of my dear relative is spilled!
sentences.ko: 오, 영주님! 오, 여보! 소중한 우리 친척의 피가 흘렀어요!

sentences.en: Prince, if you are fair, shed Montague blood for ours.
sentences.ko: 영주님, 공정하시다면 우리 피의 대가로 몬태규의 피를 흘리게 해 주세요.

sentences.en: O cousin, cousin.
sentences.ko: 아, 조카야, 조카야.

speaker: PRINCE
raw: Benvolio, who began this bloody fray?

sentences.en: Benvolio, who started this bloody fight?
sentences.ko: 벤볼리오, 이 피비린내 나는 싸움을 누가 시작했느냐?

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
Tybalt, here slain, whom Romeo’s hand did slay;
Romeo, that spoke him fair, bid him bethink
How nice the quarrel was, and urg’d withal
Your high displeasure. All this uttered
With gentle breath, calm look, knees humbly bow’d
Could not take truce with the unruly spleen
Of Tybalt, deaf to peace, but that he tilts
With piercing steel at bold Mercutio’s breast,
Who, all as hot, turns deadly point to point,
And, with a martial scorn, with one hand beats
Cold death aside, and with the other sends
It back to Tybalt, whose dexterity
Retorts it. Romeo he cries aloud,
‘Hold, friends! Friends, part!’ and swifter than his tongue,
His agile arm beats down their fatal points,
And ’twixt them rushes; underneath whose arm
An envious thrust from Tybalt hit the life
Of stout Mercutio, and then Tybalt fled.
But by and by comes back to Romeo,
Who had but newly entertain’d revenge,
And to’t they go like lightning; for, ere I
Could draw to part them was stout Tybalt slain;
And as he fell did Romeo turn and fly.
This is the truth, or let Benvolio die.

sentences.en: Tybalt is lying here, and Romeo's hand killed him.
sentences.ko: 티볼트가 여기 누워 있으며, 로미오의 손에 죽었습니다.

sentences.en: Romeo spoke to him nicely and told Tybalt how bad the fight was.
sentences.ko: 로미오는 그에게 친절하게 말하며 싸움이 얼마나 험악한지 티볼트에게 말했습니다.

sentences.en: He warned him about your anger with a gentle voice and a calm look.
sentences.ko: 부드러운 목소리와 차분한 얼굴로 영주님의 노여움을 상기시켰습니다.

sentences.en: He even bowed humbly, but Tybalt did not listen to peace.
sentences.ko: 그는 겸허하게 고개까지 숙였으나, 티볼트는 화해의 말을 듣지 않았습니다.

sentences.en: Tybalt had an angry temper and attacked Mercutio's chest with a sharp sword.
sentences.ko: 티볼트는 성격이 급해 날카로운 칼로 머큐쇼의 가슴을 공격했습니다.

sentences.en: Mercutio was also very angry, so he fought back with his sword.
sentences.ko: 머큐쇼도 매우 화가 나서 칼로 맞서 싸웠습니다.

sentences.en: He pushed death away with one hand and sent the attack back to Tybalt with the other.
sentences.ko: 그는 한 손으로 죽음을 막아내고 다른 손으로 티볼트에게 반격했습니다.

sentences.en: Tybalt blocked the move skillfully while Romeo shouted, 'Stop, friends! Friends, break it up!'
sentences.ko: 로미오가 '멈춰라, 친구들아! 친구들아, 그만해!'라고 외치는 동안 티볼트는 기술적으로 그 공격을 막았습니다.

sentences.en: His arm moved faster than his words as he pushed their swords down.
sentences.ko: 말보다 빠르게 팔을 뻗어 두 사람의 칼을 쳐 내렸습니다.

sentences.en: He ran between them, but under his arm, a sneaky thrust from Tybalt struck brave Mercutio.
sentences.ko: 그러고는 둘 사이로 뛰어들었는데, 그의 팔 밑으로 티볼트의 비겁한 찌르기가 용감한 머큐쇼를 찔렀습니다.

sentences.en: Then Tybalt ran away, but in a moment, he came back to Romeo.
sentences.ko: 그러고는 티볼트가 도망쳤다가, 곧 로미오에게 되돌아왔습니다.

sentences.en: Romeo had just started to seek revenge, and they fought like lightning.
sentences.ko: 로미오가 막 복수를 시작하려던 찰나, 그들은 번개처럼 싸웠습니다.

sentences.en: Before I could move to separate them, Tybalt was killed.
sentences.ko: 제가 그들을 떼어놓기 위해 움직이기 전에 티볼트가 죽었습니다.

sentences.en: As he fell, Romeo turned and ran away.
sentences.ko: 티볼트가 쓰러지자 로미오는 돌아서서 달아났습니다.

sentences.en: This is the truth; if it is not true, let me die.
sentences.ko: 이것이 진실입니다. 만약 사실이 아니라면 저를 죽여 주십시오.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
He is a kinsman to the Montague.
Affection makes him false, he speaks not true.
Some twenty of them fought in this black strife,
And all those twenty could but kill one life.
I beg for justice, which thou, Prince, must give;
Romeo slew Tybalt, Romeo must not live.

sentences.en: He is a relative of the Montague family.
sentences.ko: 저 아이는 몬태규 집안의 친척입니다.

sentences.en: Love makes him dishonest, so he does not speak the truth.
sentences.ko: 정에 끌려 거짓을 말하니, 진실이 아닙니다.

sentences.en: About twenty people fought in this terrible fight, but they could only kill one person.
sentences.ko: 스무 명쯤이 이 끔찍한 싸움에 가담했는데, 겨우 한 사람만 죽였단 말입니까.

sentences.en: I ask for justice, which you must give, Prince.
sentences.ko: 영주님, 정의를 구합니다. 반드시 내려 주십시오.

sentences.en: Romeo killed Tybalt, so Romeo must not live.
sentences.ko: 로미오가 티볼트를 죽였으니, 로미오도 살려 두어서는 안 됩니다.

speaker: PRINCE
raw:
Romeo slew him, he slew Mercutio.
Who now the price of his dear blood doth owe?

sentences.en: Romeo killed him.
sentences.ko: 로미오가 그를 죽였다.

sentences.en: He killed Mercutio.
sentences.ko: 그는 머큐쇼를 죽였다.

sentences.en: Who now owes the price for his dear blood?
sentences.ko: 이제 누가 그의 소중한 피에 대한 대가를 치러야 하는가?

speaker: MONTAGUE

sentences.en: Not Romeo, Prince.
sentences.ko: 영주님, 로미오가 아닙니다.

sentences.en: He was Mercutio's friend.
sentences.ko: 그는 머큐쇼의 친구였습니다.

sentences.en: His crime only ended what the law would have ended anyway: Tybalt's life.
sentences.ko: 그 애의 죄는 법이 어차피 끝냈을 티볼트의 목숨을 끝낸 것뿐입니다.

speaker: PRINCE
raw:
And for that offence
Immediately we do exile him hence.
I have an interest in your hate’s proceeding,
My blood for your rude brawls doth lie a-bleeding.
But I’ll amerce you with so strong a fine
That you shall all repent the loss of mine.
I will be deaf to pleading and excuses;
Nor tears nor prayers shall purchase out abuses.
Therefore use none. Let Romeo hence in haste,
Else, when he is found, that hour is his last.
Bear hence this body, and attend our will.
Mercy but murders, pardoning those that kill.

sentences.en: For that crime, we exile him: he must leave this city at once.
sentences.ko: 그 죄로 우리는 그를 추방한다. 그는 즉시 이 도시를 떠나야 한다.

sentences.en: Your hatred has hurt me personally.
sentences.ko: 너희의 증오가 나에게 직접적인 상처를 입혔다.

sentences.en: My blood is bleeding because of your rude fight.
sentences.ko: 너희의 무도한 싸움 때문에 내 핏줄이 피를 흘리고 있다.

sentences.en: But I will fine you so heavily that you will all be sorry for my loss.
sentences.ko: 그러나 무거운 벌금을 물려, 너희 모두 내 혈육을 잃게 한 것을 후회하게 하겠다.

sentences.en: I will not listen to pleas or excuses.
sentences.ko: 나는 애원이나 변명을 듣지 않겠다.

sentences.en: Neither tears nor prayers will change the punishment.
sentences.ko: 눈물도 기도도 형벌을 바꾸지 못할 것이다.

sentences.en: So do not use them.
sentences.ko: 그러니 그것들을 쓰지 마라.

sentences.en: Let Romeo leave here quickly.
sentences.ko: 로미오는 서둘러 이곳을 떠나게 하라.

sentences.en: If he is found, that hour will be his last.
sentences.ko: 그가 발견된다면, 그 시간은 그의 마지막이 될 것이다.

sentences.en: Take this body away.
sentences.ko: 이 시신을 치워라.

sentences.en: Follow my orders.
sentences.ko: 내 명령을 따르라.

sentences.en: Mercy that forgives killers only causes more murder.
sentences.ko: 살인자를 용서하는 자비는 더 많은 살인만을 불러올 뿐이다.

raw: Exeunt.
